match.reason: The closest bank point, Measuring inflation (e-cpi), does define inflation, disinflation and deflation, but its main subject is how CPI is measured, weighted and limited, which is broader than the brief's three definitions, so a new point is the better fit.

draft.title: Inflation, disinflation and deflation
card: Inflation
a sustained rise in the general price level. Prices on average are higher than before.
Disinflation
a fall in the rate of inflation. Prices are still rising, but more slowly than before.
Deflation
a sustained fall in the general price level. Prices on average are lower than before, so the inflation rate is negative.
Look at the direction of the price level first. If it is rising, it is inflation or disinflation. If it is falling, it is deflation.
draft.remember: Inflation is prices rising. Disinflation is prices still rising, but more slowly. Deflation is prices falling.

a.q: Annual inflation in a country falls from 6% to 4%. What has happened?
opts: Disinflation, as prices still rise but more slowly
Deflation, as the inflation rate has fallen
Disinflation, as the general price level has fallen
Inflation, as the rate of price rises has slowed
a.why: The rate fell, but it is still above zero, so prices are still rising. That is disinflation. Deflation is tempting because the rate fell, but it needs the price level itself to fall.
a.clue: Is the price level still going up?

b.q: Last year the price index in Country X rose by 3%. This year it fell by 1%. What does this show?
opts: Deflation, as the general price level fell
Disinflation, as the inflation rate fell
Inflation, as the price index changed
Disinflation, as price rises have slowed to zero
b.why: A fall of 1% means prices on average are lower, which is deflation. Disinflation is tempting because the rate dropped from 3% to -1%, but disinflation means prices are still rising, just more slowly.
b.clue: Check whether the price level is rising or falling this year.

a.best: Disinflation, as prices still rise but more slowly

b.best: Deflation, as the general price level fell
also_right: Disinflation, as the inflation rate fell

problems.detail: The card first defines disinflation as 'a fall in the rate of inflation', and the rate did fall from 3% to -1%. So 'Disinflation, as the inflation rate fell' fits that first clause literally. The card's later bullets settle it as deflation, but the question would be firmer if the distractor's reason were plainly false, or if the card's definition said 'while the rate stays positive'.
